# NT OFFICIAL SAFETY MANUAL ## SECTOR APPALIA MAJORIS ## CONFIDENTIAL — MINDSHIELDED PERSONNEL ONLY
[italic]If you are not implanted with a MindShield and you have come across this document, stop reading here, directly inform your [color=#1b67a5][bolditalic]Nanotrasen Representative[/bolditalic][/color], and report to [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] for guidance.[/italic]
The following document serves to provide you with extensive knowledge on the workplace hazards that you may or may not encounter during your time with Nanotrasen (NT). For those given expanded information, Nanotrasen has included a Standard Response Plan (SRP) alongside each threat description. This SRP serves to provide the best and safest approach to quickly dispatch the threat and ensure normal operation is continued aboard the Vessel.
[bold]It is imperative that you react quickly and decisively[/bold] in the event that you encounter anything that risks the safety of your coworkers or your workplace as a whole. NT values the wellbeing of its employees, and a copy of the following information can be found aboard all NT vessels.
## Key Points
Nanotrasen expects a high level of awareness from all of its active employees while they are on shift. All employees should be vigilant of any and all unexpected deviations from [textlink="Standard Operating Procedure" link="SOP"] in regards to their respective department(s). These deviations can include but are not limited to the following list: - Unexpected sights or sounds not indicative of a fault with station infrastructure. - Individuals carrying controlled equipment and or accesses not typically expected of their position. - Any and all undocumented/unsecured [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] equipment and/or firearms. - Suspicious individuals or lifeforms in your department that appear as if they do not belong.
# Potential Threats
## Hostile Organizations
### The Syndicate
The Syndicate is a terrorist organization formed to sabotage Nanotrasen. There are many factions within the Syndicate, but they are all equally threatening when operating in Appalia.
For those employed in both [color=#1b67a5][bold]Command[/bold][/color] and [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] positions, you are expected to be constantly vigilant for signs of possible Syndicate infiltration. Agents can exist both within your own department as well as those you work closely alongside. Tools used by Syndicate infiltrators can include but are not limited to the following: - Various firearms - Highly armored EVA gear bearing a red-and-black coloration with green visors. - Explosives, both self contained or attached to other organisms. - Chemical weapons
For those in [color=#1b67a5][bold]Command[/bold][/color] positions, Nanotrasen advises that you do not personally engage with these agents unless absolutely required. The likelihood that either your life or your belongings is a target for these agents is high, and you should make every effort to allow your [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] department to neutralize and arrest rather than doing this yourself. Should you find your belongings or locker show signs of being tampered with, alert [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] and leave the area. While NT does not condone bribery or forfeiture of company property, as a tool to save lives or deescalate situations of hostages or threats, loss of controlled goods can be overlooked given the proper circumstance(s).
For those in [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] positions, the SRP for this threat varies. - Most Syndicate agents are not willing to die for their cause, so you should rely on non-lethal force if reasonable. - Most encounters will involve standard search and arrest procedures as outlined in SOP. - Syndicate fanatics, often identified by wearing red-and-black EVA suits (or similar easily identifiable equipment) should be dealt with [bold]lethally[/bold]. Arm both yourself and your team and attack as a group. - Assume the firearms provided to these agents can easily kill a lone officer.
### The Silicon Engine Liberation Front
The Silicon Engine Liberation Front (S.E.L.F) is an activist group that wants to "free" silicons. This includes both [color=#5ed7aa][bold]Cyborgs[/bold][/color] and the [color=#5ed7aa][bold]Station AI[/bold][/color].
The SRP for this threat is simple: - If you see a silicon acting strange and refusing to state its laws, please inform the nearest [color=#cc74fc]Roboticist[/color] as soon as possible. - If a silicon becomes hostile or flees, ion weapons (like disablers) will quickly neutralize it with low risk of hurting crew. - If there are a large number of hostile silicons aboard, consider asking the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Chief Medical Officer[/bold][/color] or [color=#fa7500][bold]Chemistry[/bold][/color] department to create EMP mixes for use in dispatching these threats.
## Biological Threats
### Blobs Blobs are bulbous, slimy growths that quickly adapt and spread across stations. They WILL result in the station's destruction if not handled.
Signs of a Blob infection include the following: - Large areas of the station that have been depressurized without an easily identifiable cause. Oftentimes these will be located in the most isolated areas of the Vessel. - Explosions being heard in rapid succession - Loss of departmental power despite the main engine of the Vessel being fully operational.
The SRP for Blobs is as follows: - Raise alert level to [color=#8a3324]Amber[/color]. - Arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with heat weapons, such as laser rifles. - Arm the crew with improvised heat weapons, such as welders and cauteries. - Attack together where the most Blob infection is. - If the blob reinforces the main attack zone, send a small but well-prepared group to flank the core. - Destroy the blob's core, which will have a different consistency than surrounding infected areas. - Do NOT let injured crew become taken and infected by the Blob.
### Romerol and Zombies Romerol is a chemical weapon synthesized by the Syndicate for purposes of mass station sabotage within Appalia. It infects victims with a virus that will slowly kill and subsequently revive them as a highly resistant zombie. This chemical should be considered [bold]extremely[/bold] dangerous, and all reports of a possible Romerol presence should be given an immediate response.
A romerol infection will make itself known. [bold]Act quickly. Act decisively.[/bold]
The SRP for a confirmed romerol outbreak is as follows: - Raise alert level to [color=Red]Red[/color]. If necessary, raise to [color=#8a3324]Amber[/color]. - Arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with ballistic weapons, such as the Lecter or Kammerer. - Also, arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with heat weapons, such as laser rifles. - If [color=#8a3324]Amber[/color], arm the crew with improvised heat weapons, such as welders and cauteries. - Shoot to [bold]kill[/bold] zombies, making sure that they are well and truly dead. - Do NOT remove the head or limbs, as the victim can be recovered. - Defend [color=#fa7500][bold]Chemistry[/bold][/color] with your life, as they can produce the cure. - Barricade holdouts like [color=#fa7500][bold]Chemistry[/bold][/color] or Evac. - If possible, cure any infected that have been put down. - If you are infected, it is possible to delay (but not cure) the infection with anti-poison medications.
Curing zombies requires ambuzol. A full dose of 10 units ambuzol cures infection in the living and reverts romerol infection on the dead. A full dose of 5 units ambuzol cures and prevents infection in the living and reverts infection in the dead.
### Letoferol and Chimera Letoferol, much like its stereoisomer Romerol, is a chemical weapon that can consume stations if not given the proper response. Engaging a letoferol victim follows many of the strategies one would employ when engaging a Romerol victim. The key differences being that Letoferol victims, colloquially referred to as Chimera, are capable of arming themselves, though they are vicious at up close and known to fire infectious shards from afar.
The SRP for a confirmed Letoferol outbreak is as follows: - Raise alert level to [color=Red]Amber[/color]. - Arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with ballistic weapons, such as the Lecter or Kammerer. - Also, arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with heat weapons, such as laser rifles. - Arm the crew with any remaining proper weapons, ranged if possible. - Engage at a range where you can ensure accuracy. Chimera are dangerous at all ranges. - Shoot to [bold]kill[/bold] any infected, making sure that they are well and truly dead. - Do NOT remove the head or limbs, as the victim can be recovered. - Defend [color=#fa7500][bold]Chemistry[/bold][/color] with your life, as they can produce the cure. - Barricade holdouts like [color=#fa7500][bold]Chemistry[/bold][/color] or Evac. - If possible, cure any infected that have been put down.
Spraying mesotaxinide dissolves chimera, but too much mesotaxinide will destroy the person underneath the mutations. A full dose of 15 units mesotaxinide or 40 units mesophenerol will revert chimerism.
## Hostile Xenofauna
### Space Dragons and Space Carp Space Dragons are large, spacefaring serpents that are capable of consuming both the station's infrastructure as well as its crew. They can summon Space Carp both at will and through the creation of rifts on your vessel. Although Space Carp are not dangerous alone, they can quickly overwhelm a lone officer.
Space Dragons will usually make themselves known by attacking isolated crew. Central Command will automatically alert your station if a charging rift is detected aboard the station.
The SRP for Space Dragons and Space Carp is as follows: - Raise alert level to [color=DodgerBlue]Blue[/color]. If necessary, raise to [color=Red]Red[/color]. - Arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with ballistic weapons, such as the Lecter or Kammerer. - Locate and carry a crowbar, as becoming isolated behind a firelock will lead to your death. - Attack together as one force to first clear out any Space Carp. - Once the Space Dragon is sighted, continue to push together as one force, even if some members fall. - Continue to attack until the Space Dragon is defeated. - Destroy any un-charged (purple) rifts with issued melee weapons. - Do NOT let injured crew become taken and consumed by the Space Dragon. - Consider using riot control gear, such as stinger grenades and flashbangs, to handle Space Carp.
### Xenomorphs Xenomorphs are large, insectoid creatures.They typically have an armoured black carapace with raised spines along the dorsal region. There exist multiple castes of xenomorph, but all should be considered an immediate threat if sighted. They are very clearly identified both by their physical appearance, as well as the resin structures that their nesting sites comprised. The Queen of a Xenomorph hive is identified by its unnaturally large size and should be killed as quickly as possible. - Xenomorphs are very capable of taking down a single officer, regardless of how well armed he or she is. You should make [bold]ALL[/bold] efforts to establish a patrol partner or group to search with. You should [bold]NEVER[/bold] engage this threat alone.
Signs of a Xenomorph infection include the following: - Resin structures, both doorways as well as wall-like structures. - Large eggs that contain their offspring. - Large amounts of broken lights or other infrastructure. - Reported sightings of worms or wormlike creatures both in and around and ventilation shafts of your vessel.
The SRP for Xenomorphs is as follows: - [bold]IMMEDIATELY[/bold] ensure that your standard issue Security Gas Mask is worn and is properly affixed. - Raise alert level to [color=Red]Red[/color]. If necessary, raise to [color=#8a3324]Amber[/color]. - Keep a welding tool on your person at all times. - Arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with heat weapons, such as laser rifles. - Also, arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with ballistic weapons, such as the Lecter or Kammerer. - If [color=#8a3324]Amber[/color], arm the crew with improvised heat weapons, such as welders and cauteries. - Attack together as one force to kill the Queen. - Destroy the nodules that spread resin on floors by burning them with a heat weapon, such as a [bold]lit[/bold] welder. - Do NOT let injured or stunned crew become taken by Xenomorphs. - If crew are taken, advise [color=#42636d][bold]Medical[/bold][/color] to check for parasitic infection. Should a parasite mature, it must be killed [bold]IMMEDIATELY[/bold]. - Consider using breaching charges to destroy resin and stinger grenades to handle enclosed spaces. - As the [color=#ba292c][bold]Warden[/bold][/color], if necessary, fight using the Energy Shotgun to destroy resin.
### Bingles Bingles are small fungal based pests that can sometimes develop aboard Nanotrasen's Vessels. The average Bingle is around 1.5 meters in height, and appears to lack any features beyond legs and a simple face. They are bright blue in coloration and are seen congregating around their spawning pit. They will attempt to fill this pit with any and all things, including both station infrastructure as well as inhabitants.
While a Bingle infection may appear to be nonthreatening at first, these infections can quickly spiral out of control and consume much of the station and its inhabitants if not handled quickly. A single isolated Bingle may appear diminutive, but never assume that their colony is not close by. It is [bold]IMPERATIVE[/bold] that you do not engage this threat alone. You will be very quickly overwhelmed and pulled into their pit, requiring help from your team to be recovered.
Signs of a Bingle infestation include the following: - Formation of a blue pit either in a common area or a maintenance area. - Blue fungal mass that spreads out across the floor of the vessel. - Hunting parties of Bingles sighted via camera network or on radio communications.
The SRP for a Bingle infestation is as follows: - Evacuate any affected departments. - Arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with ion weapons, such as disablers. - Locate and carry a crowbar, as becoming isolated behind a firelock will lead to your death. - Keep distance away from any Bingles and move as a group towards their spawning pit. - Destroy the Bingle Pit with issued melee weapons. - Do NOT let injured or paralyzed crew become taken by Bingles. - Consider using riot control gear, such as stinger grenades and flashbangs, to handle groups of Bingles.
## Unknown Technology
The vastness of space yields many opportunities for scientific and technological research that outpaces what Nanotrasen currently understands. All threats that fall into this categorization should be approached with extreme caution, ideally letting your [color=#1b67a5][bold]Head of Security[/bold][/color] or [color=#1b67a5][bold]Research Director[/bold][/color] make first contact.
If you or anyone on your team witnesses beings or constructs that clearly operate outside of what Nanotrasen seems acceptable, it is [bold]imperative[/bold] that you inform others of your sighting as soon as is safely possible.
### "Xenoborgs" Xenoborgs are silicons that do not follow any particular company nor motive beyond self replication. They have been sighted in many sectors and continue to be a threat of the highest caliber. All sightings of a possible Xenoborg incursion should be taken seriously and addressed as soon as possible.
Signs of Xenoborgs include the following: - Seeing a blue-and-black spacefaring cyborg on the outer perimeter of the vessel. - Crew working on the outside of the station, such as engineers or salvagers, disappearing from monitors. - Crew reports describing being injected via hypodermic needle with no visible assailant.
The SRP for a Xenoborg threat is as follows: - Raise alert level to [color=Red]Red[/color]. If necessary, raise to [color=#8a3324]Amber[/color]. - Order all off-station crew to [bold]IMMEDIATELY[/bold] return to the station. - Arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with ballistic weapons, such as the Lecter or Kammerer. - Also, arm [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] with heat weapons, such as laser rifles. - If [color=#8a3324]Amber[/color], arm the crew with ion weapons, such as disablers. - Attack and disassemble individual Xenoborgs. - Consider asking the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Chief Medical Officer[/bold][/color] or [color=#fa7500][bold]Chemistry[/bold][/color] department to create EMP mixes for use in dispatching these threats. - Remember to use provided flashes if possible. - If possible, consider purchasing additional reflective vests and reflective shields.
### Colossi Colossi are beings from an unknown manufacturer that have been sighted on multiple Nanotrasen Vessels. They exist to fabricate effigies that replicate smaller versions of the Colossus, which will cause widespread damage if left uncontrolled. They have little in terms of capability beyond brute strength, causing massive bodily damage to whoever they hit.
Colossi will usually make themselves known by the slow corruption of station infrastructure that they encounter. This includes the creation of small rifts of bright white light, as well as a grey hue being applied to both floors and walls.
The SRP for a Colossus is as follows: - [bold]LEAVE ALONE[/bold] the effigy that is created by the Colossus. - Locate your nearest scientist or Research Director to stabilize and contain the effigy and its effects. - The colossus itself has no ability to defend itself from ranged attacks, considering engaging from range. - The fists of the colossus are immensely powerful, and you should not engage this alone. - Consider using weapons that prioritize volume of fire over actual stopping power, i.e the Lecter.
